thread:
ops-bot: 🚨 ALERT: gpu-23 has hit a sustained burst of Xid=13/Correctable ECC before driver reset. 18 driver resets in last 10m, container restarts increasing. Auto-esc to #incidents.

maria: seeing the same graphs in infra-dash. ECC correctable count spiking on GPU0/1 -> NVLINK lane errors?

ashwin: confirmed. telemetry shows ECC corrections per-sec ramping to 600+ on gpu-23:0. dmesg shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13` followed by `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus`.

julia: tagging oncall. is this customer-impacting? any 5xx from inference API?

maria: yes, a small subset of requests hitting dedicated pool backed by gpu-23 are getting 502/503. Overall p50 unaffected but p99 spikes from 120ms -> 1.4s and increase in tail errors.

samir: quick mitigation idea: cordon gpu-23, drain pods running on the node (prefer graceful), and failover to standby pool. Willing to take the execution if others agree.

ashwin: agree. but draining will cause batch jobs to be rescheduled—we should limit disruption: run `kubectl drain gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector=app=inference` then scale dedicated pool up by 10% during drain.

maria: starting drain now. patching autoscaler to +1 replica for dedicated-gpu-pool.

ops-bot: ACTION TAKEN: node gpu-23 cordoned by maria. Drain initiated.

julia: ops note — customers via dedicated capacity may see brief model cold starts while pods reschedule. notify SRE on L2 if errors persist after failover.

ashwin: while drain proceeds, capturing more logs. dump of recent dmesg snippet:```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU ecc: correctable error detected
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=2234, GPU=0000:65:00
[ 1234.577000] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

maria: running nvml diagnostics remotely; output: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows correctable errors surging only on channels associated with GPU0/1. NVML indicates ECC 1.2M corrections total. Not normal.

samir: could be bad DIMM(s) on host or firmware regression. Recent host kernel update rolled 3 days ago?

len: host kernel is 6.4.8, nvdriver v515.76.09, vendor firmware 46. Looking at fleet telemetry, 3 other nodes had small bumps but nowhere near this rate.

maria: drain completed, pods rescheduled -> errors dropping from 502/503 to baseline for impacted customers. autoscaler increment applied. Monitoring p99.

ops-bot: NOTE: 502 error rate decreased by 83% after drain.

ashwin: ops-check: we should attempt a controlled driver unload/reload on gpu-23 once empty, to see if driver reset clears error flood. If not, hardware replacement.

julia: agree. prefer to avoid immediate reboot to preserve ephemeral logs; do `modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia` then `modprobe nvidia nvidia_drm nvidia_uvm` and watch dmesg for reappearance.

maria: proceeding with unload/reload. node is empty. take note: will put node in maintenance.

ops-bot: ACTION TAKEN: node gpu-23 put into maintenance by maria.

maria: unload sequence produced this in dmesg:```
[ 1250.123456] nvidia: module has 0 fans attached, unloading
[ 1250.125000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=0, GPU=0000:65:00
[ 1250.130000] NVRM: GPU unplugged unexpectedly during driver unload
```

samir: sad. then reload: after modprobe we see immediate Xid 13 flood again. driver alone didn't clear it -> strongly suggests hardware ECC unit saturation or persistent memory faults.

len: next step: schedule powercycle of host or SOB (soft reboot of GPU bus). But because this is a dedicated host with customer workloads, we should coordinate with hardware ops for cold-reboot or RMA.

ashwin: recommend raising a hardware ticket and moving node to quarantine. mark host as `evacuation-required` so orchestrator won't schedule there. prepare RMA if vendor confirms ECC DIMM fault.

julia: creating incident bridge with hardware ops and support to draft customer comms. we should include timeline, affected customer list, and mitigation steps (failover + autoscaler).

maria: noting affected customers in thread: cust-alpha (dedicated pool), cust-gamma (small fraction), internal loadtests. Will open PSR with support.

ops-bot: BRIDGE CREATED: #incidents-3698765432-bridge. Participants: infra-hw, hw-support, cust-eng.

samir: hardware ops asks for memory ECC dump + SMART + `systool -v` outputs — collecting artifacts and pushing to S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/incident-3698765432/

maria: uploaded nvme SMART + nvml logs + host journal. link: https://s3.console.aws/incident-3698765432 (internal).

len: hardware ops says if powercycle doesn't fix, plan RMA. They also flagged a similar failure last month on same rack; vendor wants serial logs.

julia: customer comm draft in #cust-comms-drafts. TL;DR: brief disruption for a small set of dedicated customers, mitigation applied (pods failed over), ongoing maintenance for gpu-23, potential host replacement.

ashwin: runbook action item: add a temporary scheduling rule to prefer healthy nodes with ECC-corrected rate < 1000/hour for critical pools until hardware patch/firmware is confirmed.

maria: livecheck — p99 now back to baseline and error rates low for affected pools. marking short-term mitigation successful.

ops-bot: METRIC: ECC correctables on gpu-23 dropped to 0 after drain and maintenance.

samir: next steps: 1) keep node quarantined 2) schedule hardware ops for powercycle 3) if powercycle fails, RMA 4) postmortem in 72h with telemetry + timeline.

julia: oncall-bot, please hand this to next shift with notes.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: incident 3698765432 -> next-oncall. Summary: ECC saturation on gpu-23 caused repeated Xid=13 driver resets and customer 502s. Node drained and quarantined; failed driver reload suggests hardware fault. Artifacts uploaded. Contact infra-hw for RMA.

maria: leaving detailed runbook steps in incident doc. tagging @len for firmware follow-up.

len: noted. will add fleet patch check to ensure no widespread regression.

julia: closing the realtime paging loop. leaving incident bridge open until hardware confirms powercycle outcome.

ops-bot: STATUS: monitoring continues. If new driver resets observed, reopen page.

maria: thanks everyone. moving to post-incident actions after hardware ops completes.
